paragraphs: Judgment center: the work of education and childcare administrators for preschool and daycare (US O*NET-SOC 11-9031.00 Education and Childcare Administrators, Preschool and Daycare) is to turn these upstream conditions—the mission and regulations of the preschool or daycare institution, the needs of enrolled children and parents and staff, childcare and education curriculum and safety and health data, and funding and budgets and premises and facilities and personnel qualifications and filing—into executable, verifiable, and accountable childcare and operating results: first set the childcare and education curriculum and safety and health and staffing objectives per the institution's mission and regulations and child development principles, then recruit, train, and evaluate teachers and childcare and health care staff and organize daily life and play and activities, then communicate with parents and establish a parent committee and information disclosure, meanwhile prepare and execute budgets and apply for funding and subsidies and arrange premises and facilities and food and hygiene and safety, then liaise with the education or health authorities and the community and handle licensing and registration and filing and assessment, and finally adjust plans according to data and feedback and complete the handover. The key judgment is not whether you can control people, but whether you can hold the four things—child safety, qualification compliance, funding transparency, and record traceability—along the chain of childcare and safety and health, personnel and parents and community, and funding and compliance and licensing, and leave a verifiable record at every step.

Suitable to try first: willing to be responsible for children's safety and health and development results and to accept questioning from parents, staff, and the competent department; able to switch rhythm among childcare and education, personnel, funding, and safety; willing to work within regulations and licensing and filing and health and safety requirements and handle child health and safety and complaint matters; and able to accept longer hours and on-site duty driven by enrollment and term start and assessment and inspection and funding cycles.

Choose with caution: if you expect this work to be only looking after children or to discuss only curriculum without funding and personnel and safety, or you are unwilling to work within regulations and licensing and filing and health and safety requirements, avoid child safety and qualification and funding and hygiene responsibility, treat experience as a conclusion and make major decisions on that basis, or find it hard to keep patience and professional boundaries under a high-intensity on-site setting, parent communication, and inspections, then the actual work experience will usually not match expectations.

Low-risk check: use the fictional institutional material and anonymous funding and personnel data provided on this page to complete one paper exercise of writing a childcare and safety and health improvement plan's performance goals and measures and data basis and funding and compliance verification; it only checks whether you are willing to verify item by item against goals, data, and regulations and to mark uncertainty truthfully. The exercise uses fictional material, draws no medical, legal, financial, or personnel discipline conclusions, and is not equivalent to kindergarten principal or daycare institution head position training or appointment qualification.

Judgment center: whether the institution's mission and childcare and education and safety and health data and children and parents and staff needs can be turned into childcare and operating results that staff, parents, and the competent department can all take up and verify.

Work rhythm is set jointly by enrollment and term start and semesters and assessment and inspection points and the funding cycle and competent department inspections; there is more on-site duty and parent communication and safety patrol, and decisions and communication need to leave a trace.

Similar names do not mean the same duties: this page is O*NET-SOC 11-9031.00 Education and Childcare Administrators, Preschool and Daycare (education and childcare administrators for preschool and daycare). Adjacent positions—education administrators for kindergarten through secondary (11-9032), education administrators, postsecondary (11-9033), social and community service managers (11-9151), training and development managers (11-3131), preschool teachers (25-2011), childcare workers (39-9011), and nannies (39-9011.01)—have different objects and authorization; this occupation is also not the same as a preschool teacher or childcare worker. Kindergarten principal and daycare institution head appointment qualifications and engagement and filing and position training follow the jurisdiction's regulations and competent department requirements, are not inferred from the position name, and must not exceed authority to issue medical, legal, financial, or personnel discipline conclusions externally.

AI can be treated as controlled paperwork and data assistance, but generated content cannot be treated as unverified childcare plans, health and safety judgments, or funding and compliance conclusions; child and parent and staff data and external reports and discipline remain the responsibility of named responsible persons and the institution.

Fit judgment should combine whether you can be responsible for child safety and health and development, whether you can work with regulations and licensing and filing and data, whether you can communicate under a high-intensity on-site setting and parent communication and inspections and escalate per the system, and whether you are clear about your authority boundaries over child data, personnel, funding, and external reports; it is not replaced by a self-assessment of liking children or being patient, and all of this must be confirmed in supervised childcare and operations experience.

All exercises on this page use fictional material; real childcare and health and safety and personnel and funding and licensing and discipline decisions must be undertaken by personnel with the corresponding qualifications and in accordance with the jurisdiction's regulations, competent department, and institutional rules; individuals must not exceed authority to issue medical, legal, financial, or personnel discipline conclusions externally, and this page does not constitute any medical, legal, financial, or appointment advice.

The work object of this occupation is the preschool and daycare institution with high-frequency interaction among multiple parties: the institution's mission and regulations; the needs of enrolled children and parents and staff; childcare and education curriculum and daily life and play and activities; safety and health and hygiene and food and fire protection; funding and budgets and subsidies and fees; premises and facilities and toys and books and information systems; and licensing and registration and filing and assessment and inspection arrangements. The output is childcare and operating results that meet the institution's mission and regulatory requirements: childcare and education curriculum and daily life delivered per child development principles and regulations, childcare and safety and health improvement plans formed from data, recruitment and training and evaluation and qualification and filing records completed per the system, funding and procurement and premises and facilities and food and hygiene records executed per budget, and verifiable licensing and filing and assessment and disclosure records. The basis for judgment is the institution's mission, regulations, data, and competent department requirements, not personal preference or the position name.

Judgment one: whether the institution's mission and the childcare and education curriculum are aligned—whether the childcare and education curriculum and daily life and staffing objectives are determined per child development principles and regulations and assessment data, rather than making demands from impressions.

Judgment two: whether childcare observation and curriculum assessment are evidence-based—whether improvements are proposed per observations within the institution and childcare assessment and regulatory requirements, rather than judging teachers and childcare staff by personal experience.

Judgment three: whether personnel and parent communication follow the system—whether teachers and childcare and health care and security staff are recruited, trained, and evaluated per procedure and parents are communicated with and a trace kept, rather than by ad hoc decisions.

Judgment four: whether funding and fees and subsidies are held—whether preparation and execution and authorization follow the budget, funding, procurement, and fee disclosure system, rather than using funds at will.

Judgment five: whether safety and health and food and fire protection are held—whether arrangements and inspections follow the requirements for premises, facilities, food, hygiene, fire protection, and drop-off and pickup, rather than remedying things afterward.

Judgment six: whether data, compliance, licensing, external reporting, and discipline stay within boundaries—whether data use follows regulations, licensing, filing, data permissions, privacy, child information, and staff record requirements, without exceeding authority to issue medical, legal, financial, or personnel discipline conclusions externally, and with consultation and reporting per the system on anomalies.

Environment and rhythm: mainly the institution's site and offices and activity rooms and outdoor areas, with high-frequency interaction with children, parents, and staff; the rhythm is driven by enrollment and term start and semesters and assessment and inspection points and the funding cycle, with more on-site duty and parent communication and safety patrol, and decisions and communication need a trace; the specific arrangements and working hours follow the institution and jurisdiction.

The work of education and childcare administrators for preschool and daycare can be divided into three connected but independent work faces. The first is childcare and safety and health: design and assess childcare and education curriculum and daily life and play and activities per the institution's mission and child development principles and regulations, observe and guide teachers and childcare staff, ensure child safety and health and hygiene and food and fire protection and drop-off and pickup, prepare and drill emergency plans, and complete morning and afternoon checks and health observation and disinfection and isolation and records. The second is personnel and parents and community: recruit, train, and evaluate teachers and childcare and health care and security staff and handle qualifications and filing, communicate with parents about child development and daily care and establish a parent committee and open days and information disclosure, recruit and arrange volunteers and community resources, and handle complaints and disputes. The third is funding and compliance and licensing: prepare and submit budgets and funding and subsidy applications and authorize procurement and fee disclosure, arrange premises and facilities and toys and books and information systems and maintenance, interpret education or health authority regulations and handle licensing and registration and filing, accept assessment and inspection and rectify, write enrollment and publicity and report material, and supervise food and hygiene and safety and fire protection. All three work faces proceed within the institution's mission, regulations, data, and competent department requirements.
Childcare and safety and health

Determine childcare and education curriculum and daily life and staffing objectives per the institution's mission and regulations and child development principles → observe and guide teachers and childcare staff → ensure safety and health and hygiene and food and fire protection and drop-off and pickup → prepare and drill emergency plans → prepare improvement plans based on childcare and health data

Executable childcare and education curriculum and daily life and staffing objectives and improvement plans, childcare observation and assessment records, safety and health and hygiene and food and fire protection inspection and drill and rectification records, and child health observation and disinfection and isolation records
Personnel and parents and community

Recruit, train, and evaluate and handle qualifications and filing → communicate with parents and establish a parent committee and open days and information disclosure → recruit and arrange volunteers and community resources → handle complaints and disputes

Recruitment and training and evaluation and qualification and filing records, parent communication and parent committee and disclosure records, volunteer and community resource records, and complaint and handling result records
Funding and compliance and licensing

Prepare and submit budgets and funding and subsidy applications → authorize procurement and fee disclosure → arrange premises and facilities and toys and books and information systems → interpret regulations and handle licensing and registration and filing → accept assessment and inspection and rectify and write reports

When comparing, verify item by item against the service object, authorization, compliance basis, and output, and do not swap by institution or job title, nor read management duties as medical judgment authority, financial decision authority, or personnel discipline authority.
Core purpose

Turn the institution's mission and children and parents and staff needs into executable, verifiable, and accountable childcare and operating results: clear childcare and education curriculum and staffing, evidence-based safety and health and food, personnel and parents per the system, funding and premises held, and licensing and filing and reporting within boundaries.

Core purposes of adjacent positions: preschool teachers focus on class childcare and teaching itself; primary and secondary and postsecondary education administrators ensure schooling and academic affairs; social and community service managers ensure service programs and institutional operations; training and development managers improve corporate employee ability; childcare workers provide frontline care.
Main object and basis

The object is the institution's mission and regulations; enrolled children and parents and staff; childcare and education curriculum and daily life and play and activities; safety and health and hygiene and food and fire protection; funding and budgets and subsidies and fees; premises and facilities and toys and books and information systems; and licensing and registration and filing and assessment and inspection arrangements; the basis is the institution's mission, regulations, data, and competent department requirements.

Objects and bases of adjacent positions: class childcare itself (preschool education regulations and teacher professional standards); primary and secondary and postsecondary schooling and academic affairs (education regulations and institutional rules); service programs and institutional operations (social service regulations and institutional rules); corporate employees and training needs (corporate training and human resources systems); and infant and child care (childcare and care standards).
Core process

Childcare and safety and health → personnel and parents and community → funding and compliance and licensing and reporting (including childcare assessment and safety drills and inspection rectification).

Processes of adjacent positions: childcare and teaching (preschool teachers); instructional leadership—personnel and home-school relations—budget and operations (primary, secondary, and postsecondary administrators); needs assessment—program design—implementation and supervision (social and community service managers); training needs analysis—curriculum development—implementation and evaluation (training and development managers); and daily care—health observation—records (childcare workers).
Main output

Childcare and education curriculum and daily life delivered per child development principles and regulations, childcare and safety and health improvement plans formed from data, recruitment and training and evaluation and qualification and filing records completed per the system, funding and procurement and premises and facilities and food and hygiene records executed per budget, and verifiable licensing and filing and assessment and disclosure records.

Outputs of adjacent positions: class childcare and teaching records (preschool teachers); schooling and academic and compliance records (primary, secondary, and postsecondary); service program and supervision records (social and community service managers); corporate training plans and effectiveness evaluations (training and development managers); and care and health observation records (childcare workers).
Responsible party

This occupation is responsible for organizing childcare and personnel and funding and safety per the institution's mission and regulations and data and for child and parent data and reports and licensing and compliance; the sponsor and competent department bear management responsibility for licensing and funding approval and personnel discipline and compliance conclusions per regulations and systems.
Responsibilities of adjacent positions: borne by each institution's responsible persons and professionals per their own regulations and systems, with different authorization bases.
Collaboration and supervision

Collaborate with teachers and childcare and health care and security staff and parents and the parent committee and the competent department and the community and medical and fire protection staff, and adjust priorities per enrollment and term start and assessment and inspection points; child safety and health and data and funding and out-of-authority matters are consulted and reported per the system.

Collaboration of adjacent positions: with class teachers and parents (preschool teachers); with teachers and parents and supervisors (primary, secondary, and postsecondary); with the community and health and civil affairs (social and community service managers); with human resources and corporate departments (training and development managers); and with parents and health care staff (childcare workers).
Conclusion boundaries

Must determine the childcare and education curriculum and staffing per the institution's mission and regulations and data; must observe and assess childcare per the system; must recruit and evaluate and handle qualifications and filing per procedure; must prepare and execute per the budget and procurement and fee disclosure system; must arrange and inspect per the requirements for premises, facilities, food, hygiene, fire protection, and drop-off and pickup; must use child and parent and staff information per data permissions and privacy; and must not exceed authority to issue medical or legal or financial or personnel discipline conclusions externally.
The boundaries of adjacent positions are determined by their own object, regulations, and institutional rules; similar institution or job titles do not mean duties can be interchanged.
In this work, which judgments are most prone to error, and how should they be verified?

Common errors cluster in four categories: first, the institution's mission is disconnected from the childcare and education curriculum and staffing, making childcare and assessment requirements inconsistent and improvement unfounded; second, childcare and teachers are assessed by impression rather than observation and data, distorting decisions and causing staff attrition; third, personnel and parents and funding and procurement are handled without the system, procedures, and budget constraints, creating compliance, fairness, and interpersonal risks; fourth, child and parent data and reports and discipline go out of bounds or safety and health and food and fire protection are not held, creating privacy, safety, and accountability risks. The verification method is that each item has a reviewable basis: childcare curriculum and staffing and improvement plans, childcare observation and assessment records, recruitment and training and evaluation and qualification and filing records, budget and procurement and premises and facilities and food safety records, and child and parent data and reports and licensing and compliance records, rather than memory or verbal understanding.
Are the institution's mission aligned item by item with the childcare and education curriculum and staffing objectives, rather than demands made from impressions?
Are observations within the institution and childcare and curriculum assessment carried out on an evidence and regulatory basis, rather than by personal experience?
Are recruitment, training, evaluation, qualification and filing, and child health and safety handling done per procedure with a trace, rather than by ad hoc decisions?
Are budgets, funding, procurement, and fee disclosure prepared and executed and authorized per the system, rather than used at will?

Per jurisdiction and system: the appointment or engagement, appointment qualification, filing, and position training of kindergarten principals and daycare institution heads follow the Preschool Education Law of the People's Republic of China and the Standards for the Establishment of Childcare Institutions (trial) and the Management Standards for Childcare Institutions (trial) and the relevant provisions of the education or health authority, and child and parent and staff information should be used per permission and privacy requirements. Specific application follows the jurisdiction's regulations and competent department and institutional rules; this page is cited by regulation and system name and verified key points and the article numbers were not verified one by one.

Are the childcare and health and safety points with teachers and childcare and health care and security staff and parents and medical and fire protection staff completed per the system and verifiable?

Record childcare and personnel and funding and safety and hygiene and compliance data per the system and data permissions and complete the handover; records should be consistent with observation, assessment, and inspection material for ease of verification; child safety and health and data and funding and out-of-authority matters are handled per the system with a trace kept.

When a child injury or missing child or food and hygiene and fire incident, data leak, funding or procurement anomaly, qualification or discipline overreach, or out-of-authority external report occurs, is it handled in the order of first ensuring child and personnel safety and providing immediate rescue and preserving evidence, stopping the affected link, recording and reporting per the process, and involving the competent department and medical and fire and legal staff when necessary?

Core output: childcare and education curriculum and daily life delivered per child development principles and regulations, childcare and safety and health improvement plans formed from data, recruitment and training and evaluation and qualification and filing records completed per the system, funding and procurement and premises and facilities and food and hygiene records executed per budget, and verifiable licensing and filing and assessment and disclosure records.

Work environment

Mainly the institution's site and offices and activity rooms and outdoor areas, with high-frequency interaction with children, parents, and staff; the rhythm is driven by enrollment and term start and semesters and assessment and inspection points and the funding cycle, with more on-site duty and parent communication and safety patrol, and decisions and communication need a trace; the specific arrangements and working hours follow the institution and jurisdiction.

Institutional offices and activity rooms and nap rooms and dining areas and outdoor areas and the health room; work environments covering childcare and safety and health and personnel and parents and funding and compliance and reporting positions, and liaison with children, parents, staff, and the competent department.

Divided by shift group and department and program: childcare and safety and health, personnel and parents and community, and funding and compliance and licensing and reporting; coordinated by the kindergarten principal or institutional head.

Review methods include verifying childcare curriculum and staffing and improvement plans, sampling childcare observation and assessment records, verifying recruitment and training and evaluation and qualification and filing records, verifying budget and procurement and premises and facilities and food safety records, and verifying child and parent data permissions and licensing and compliance; child safety and health and data and funding anomalies are reported per the system.

Quality looks at whether the institution's mission and the childcare and education curriculum are aligned, whether observations within the institution and childcare assessment are evidence-based, whether personnel and parents and funding follow the system, whether safety and health and food and fire protection are held, and whether child and parent data and reports and licensing and compliance are verifiable.

This page corresponds exactly to US O*NET 11-9031.00 Education and Childcare Administrators, Preschool and Daycare: planning, directing, or coordinating the academic or non-academic activities of a preschool or daycare institution. The work includes determining the childcare and education curriculum and daily life and staffing objectives per the institution's mission and child development principles and regulations, observing and guiding teachers and childcare staff and assessing childcare and curriculum, ensuring child safety and health and hygiene and food and fire protection and drop-off and pickup and preparing and drilling emergency plans, communicating with parents about child development and daily care and establishing a parent committee and open days and information disclosure, recruiting, training, and evaluating teachers and childcare and health care and security staff and handling qualifications and filing, preparing and submitting budgets and funding and subsidy applications and authorizing procurement and fee disclosure, arranging premises and facilities and toys and books and information systems and maintenance, interpreting education or health authority regulations and handling licensing and registration and filing, accepting assessment and inspection and rectifying, writing enrollment and publicity and report material, and handling complaints and disputes; this is a schooling and operations management position for preschool and daycare institutions, excluding education administrators for kindergarten through secondary (11-9032), education administrators, postsecondary (11-9033), social and community service managers (11-9151), training and development managers (11-3131), preschool teachers (25-2011), childcare workers (39-9011), and nannies (39-9011.01); it does not provide medical diagnosis, legal, financial, or personnel discipline decisions.

This table compares education and childcare administrators for preschool and daycare row by row with six adjacent positions that are easily confused by institutional name and childcare management duties, or that have rotation and transfer relationships, on core work and output, key differences, and selection basis. The purpose of the comparison is not to rank them, but to explain their respective service objects, authorization, and compliance boundaries—especially that medical judgment authority, financial decision authority, and personnel discipline authority cannot all be borne by this occupation.

When comparing, rely on three things: first, the work object (primary and secondary schools and their teachers and students, colleges and their faculty and students and academic affairs, social and community service clients and institutions, corporate employees and training needs, class childcare and teaching itself, and infant and child daily care); second, the basis and authorization (the institution's mission, regulations, data, and competent department requirements; education regulations and district rules; higher education regulations and institutional rules; social service regulations and institutional rules; corporate training and human resources systems; preschool education regulations and teacher professional standards; and childcare and care standards each apply separately); third, the output and responsibility (who is responsible for the childcare and operations of a preschool and daycare institution, who for primary and secondary schooling, who for college academic and administrative affairs, who for service programs and institutional operations, who for corporate training, who for class childcare itself, and who for infant and child daily care). Where the three are inconsistent, the position's actual duties and the regulations and institutional rules prevail.

The selection basis can follow three clues: if you want to carry childcare and safety and health and personnel and funding and compliance responsibility in a preschool or daycare institution, this page's occupation is the closest; if you want to work in primary and secondary schools, colleges, social and community services, corporate training, class childcare, or frontline care, then education administrators for kindergarten through secondary, education administrators for postsecondary, social and community service managers, training and development managers, preschool teachers, and childcare workers are adjacent paths. What must be added when transferring is the object, regulations, and authorization, not only management experience.

Boundaries and sources: the differences listed in this table are based on the O*NET occupation profiles and work context data and on the names and verified key points of the Preschool Education Law and the Standards for the Establishment of Childcare Institutions (trial) and the Management Standards for Childcare Institutions (trial) of Mainland China (the rest are cited by regulation and system name and general basis, and the article numbers were not verified one by one this round). The objects, regulations, and authorization of adjacent positions cannot substitute for each other; this page does not infer income levels or hiring conditions from position names, nor does it read management duties as medical judgment authority, financial decision authority, or personnel discipline authority.
Education Administrators, Kindergarten through Secondary (11-9032.00)

Plan, direct, or coordinate the academic and administrative and auxiliary activities of kindergartens and elementary and secondary schools, responsible for primary and secondary schooling and instructional leadership and compliance.

The school stage and governance structure differ: education administrators for kindergarten through secondary serve primary and secondary schools and districts, based on compulsory education and teacher regulations and district rules; this page's occupation serves preschool institutions and daycare institutions and enrolled children and parents, based on preschool education regulations and childcare standards and competent department requirements. Both do schooling and operations, but the school stage and authorization and compliance basis differ and cannot be swapped by institution name.

If you want to carry schooling and instructional leadership in primary and secondary schools and districts, the education administrator for kindergarten through secondary direction is an option; if you want to run a preschool and daycare institution and carry childcare and safety and health responsibility, this page's occupation is closer.
Preschool Teachers (25-2011.00)
Focuses on class childcare and teaching and organizing daily life itself, responsible for concrete care and education delivery and child observation and daily parent communication.

The duty level and authorization differ: preschool teachers focus on class childcare and teaching itself and usually do not carry institution-level funding, personnel, licensing, filing, or compliance responsibility; this page's occupation carries schooling and operations and funding and personnel and licensing and filing responsibility, so the duty level and authorization differ and they cannot substitute for each other.

If you want to focus on class childcare and teaching, the preschool teacher direction is an option; if you want to carry institutional and team childcare and operations management responsibility, this page's occupation is closer.
Social and Community Service Managers (11-9151.00)

The service object and regulations differ: social and community service managers are responsible for social and community service programs and institutional operations, based on social service regulations and institutional rules; this page's occupation serves preschool institutions and daycare institutions and enrolled children and parents, based on preschool education regulations and childcare standards, and the object and compliance basis differ and cannot substitute for each other.

If you want to work in social and community service programs and institutional management, the social and community service manager direction is an option; if you want to carry childcare and operations responsibility in a preschool and daycare institution, this page's occupation is more suitable.
Training and Development Managers (11-3131.00)

The service object and basis differ: training and development managers serve corporate employees and business goals, based on corporate training and human resources systems; this page's occupation serves enrolled children and parents and staff, based on preschool education and childcare regulations and competent department requirements. Both do training and evaluation, but the object and authorization differ and cannot be swapped by department name.

If you want to do training and development in a company, the training and development manager direction is an option; if you want to carry childcare and operations responsibility in a preschool and daycare institution, this page's occupation is closer.
Education Administrators, Postsecondary (11-9033.00)

The service object and school stage differ: postsecondary education administrators are responsible for college academic and administrative affairs, based on higher education regulations and institutional rules; this page's occupation is responsible for the childcare and operations of preschool institutions and daycare institutions, and the school stage and governance structure and authorization basis differ and cannot be swapped by school stage name.

If you want to work in college academic and administrative affairs, the postsecondary education administrator direction is an option; if you want to work in preschool and daycare institution management, this page's occupation is closer.
Childcare Workers (39-9011.00)

The duties and authorization differ: childcare workers are responsible for the daily care and activity organization of infants and children and usually do not carry institution-level funding, personnel, licensing, or filing responsibility; this page's occupation carries schooling and operations and funding and personnel and licensing and filing responsibility, so the professional level and authorization differ and they cannot substitute for each other.

If you want to focus on frontline care and activity organization, the childcare worker direction is an option; if you want to carry institutional and team childcare and operations management responsibility, this page's occupation is more suitable.

subject.summary: Education and childcare administrators for preschool and daycare (US O*NET-SOC 11-9031.00, Education and Childcare Administrators, Preschool and Daycare) are the schooling and childcare and operations management positions in preschool institutions and daycare institutions: planning, directing, or coordinating the academic or non-academic activities of a preschool or daycare institution; the work includes determining the childcare curriculum and daily life and staffing objectives per the institution's mission and child development principles and regulations, observing and guiding teachers and childcare staff and assessing childcare and curriculum, ensuring child safety and health and hygiene and food and fire protection and drop-off and pickup and preparing and drilling emergency plans, completing morning and afternoon checks and health observation and disinfection and isolation and records, communicating with parents about child development and daily care and establishing a parent committee and open days and information disclosure, recruiting, training, and evaluating teachers and childcare and health care and security staff and handling qualifications and filing, preparing and submitting budgets and funding and subsidy applications and authorizing procurement and fee disclosure, arranging premises and facilities and toys and books and information systems and maintenance, interpreting education or health authority regulations and handling licensing and registration and filing, accepting assessment and inspection and rectifying and writing reports, and handling complaints and disputes. US basis: the BLS 2025 wage data median is 59,300 US dollars per year (28.51 US dollars per hour; that source provides only the median and does not provide the 10/25/75/90 percentiles); the O*NET summary page gives about 90,200 employed in 2024, a 2024—2034 projection of Decline (Decline, -1% or lower), and about 5,500 projected openings for 2024—2034 (projection-period total basis); the preparation level is Job Zone Four (SVP 7.0 to below 8.0), the education feedback is 44% bachelor's degree and 23% associate or two-year degree and 13% high school diploma or equivalent, the interest code is SEC, and there are 17 tasks. Mainland China basis: the appointment or engagement, appointment qualification, filing, and position training of kindergarten principals and childcare institution heads follow the Preschool Education Law of the People's Republic of China and the Standards for the Establishment of Childcare Institutions (trial) and the Management Standards for Childcare Institutions (trial) and the relevant provisions of the education or health authority, and kindergarten teachers should obtain the kindergarten teacher qualification. Public statistics have no occupation-level wage basis corresponding to this occupation established, and this page truthfully keeps the gap, with the industry average wage serving only as a visible industry proxy.
